# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45 (Bi-Vb Pc45)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45, titled *Adhikaraṇa* ("Not resolving a legal issue"), concerns an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) when a nun undertakes to resolve a legal issue but subsequently makes no effort to do so [SuttaCentral]. As analyzed by Ute Hüsken, the rule was established to prevent nuns from rashly taking on obligations—specifically the settlement of a legal issue or dispute—which they subsequently cannot or will not fulfill, sharing a functional purpose with Pācittiya 79 [Hüsken 1997]. In the word-commentary (*padabhājana*), the text defines an *adhikaraṇa* by outlining the four standard types of legal issues: disputes (*vivādādhikaraṇa*), accusations (*anuvādādhikaraṇa*), offenses (*āpattādhikaraṇa*), and duties or formal acts (*kiccādhikaraṇa*), which the *Samantapāsādikā* notes is provided simply to illustrate the classification of legal matters [Hüsken 1997].

According to SuttaCentral, full parallels to this rule exist across the Vinaya traditions of various schools, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 111), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 138), Mūlasarvāstivāda in both Chinese and Tibetan recensions (Bi Vb Pc 148 / Pc 162), Mahāsāṅghika (Bi Vb Pc 125), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikkhunī Vinaya* (san-lo-bi-vb-pc125), in addition to the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 593 Pali text-reuse matches across 92 works, showing prominent shared phraseology with numerous other Bhikkhunī Pācittiya rules (such as Bi-Vb Pc 23, Pc 25, Pc 33, Pc 34, Pc 77, and Pc 78), the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), and Vinaya sub-commentaries including the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignment between segment §2.1.8 and the Tibetan *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].
